A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoGuide by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved into the reorganized supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments, parameter and CFG++ ablations, inference timings, qualitative examples, and a 30-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds low-pass-filter experiments, Open-Sora evaluations, and quantitative and qualitative UniCtrl comparisons.

M1.justification: The original interpolation, renoising, filtering, and self/external guidance procedures remain; Algorithms 1 and 2 are unchanged. Supplement F adds a velocity-based rectified-flow adaptation, with a corresponding inference update in Equation 18. The rewritten main derivation does not establish a replacement of the original DDIM procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions specify text-to-video evaluation using 800 prompts from VBench categories. Open-Sora adds model and scheduler configurations, without documenting a new dataset, task, population, or input scenario. The personalized-model domains and original qualitative galleries are retained.

E2.justification: The original AnimateDiff/LaVie comparisons with FreeInit remain. v3 adds UniCtrl and the UniCtrl-plus-VideoGuide combination to the AnimateDiff comparison in Table 7. Table 2 also adds unguided baseline timings to the existing timing comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds RAFT-based dynamic degree as a fifth evaluation metric. New experiments introduce Open-Sora DiT configurations with DDIM and rectified-flow schedulers, filter-versus-no-filter controls over a longer interpolation sweep, and UniCtrl with motion injection degree 0.2. The original 800-prompt, 50-step DDIM evaluation settings remain documented.

E4.justification: Supplement A and Figure 5 newly isolate the low-pass filter's effects on consistency, imaging quality, and efficiency, extending the no-filter sweep to 50 interpolation steps. Supplements F and G add architecture/scheduler robustness and UniCtrl composability analyses. The original parameter ablations and CFG-versus-CFG++ analysis are retained, although reorganized.

E5.justification: Shared-seed qualitative comparisons remain, and neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The new filter plots show averages across prompts without introducing uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes all four AnimateDiff self-guided scores, including subject consistency from 0.9596 to 0.9520, and adds dynamic-degree results. Table 2 revises existing timings and adds baseline times. Figure 5 and Tables 6–7 introduce filter, Open-Sora, and UniCtrl findings. The original parameter-ablation, CFG++, and user-study values remain unchanged; the PDFs do not explain the revised existing scores.

T1.justification: v1 derives interpolation from a quadratic proximal objective using a temporally consistent reference latent. v3 replaces this reasoning with a teacher-denoising loss, gradient-based guidance, a different derivation of the interpolation coefficient, and a consistency-model/PF-ODE approximation in Sections 2–3. Supplement F additionally derives the rectified-flow formulation. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the central claims of training-free temporal improvement, flexible teacher guidance, and prior distillation. Sections 2–3 additionally present optimization-based video-consistency guidance as an explicit contribution and claim priority for that formulation, adding a specific novelty claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit consistency-versus-dynamic-degree trade-off, interprets filtering as accelerating convergence and preserving the student's domain, and connects excessive interpolation to SDS-related blurring. Supplement H newly states the shared-VAE-space requirement and discusses the computational and detail-loss risks of decoding and re-encoding across incompatible spaces.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies that the pseudocode uses CFG++ throughout for presentation, while the experimental implementation switches back to CFG. It documents settings for the new filter, Open-Sora, and UniCtrl experiments and changes the printed project-page address. Most original prompt-selection and hyperparameter information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands the optimization-guidance positioning through diffusion posterior sampling, decomposed diffusion sampling, score distillation, and consistency models, while removing the earlier DreamSampler citation. It also adds discussion of UniCtrl and I4VGen and references supporting DiT, rectified flow, and Open-Sora. The explicit optimization-priority claim changes its stated relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The introduction, mathematical exposition, and results discussion undergo substantial rewriting, including increased teacher/student terminology. CFG discussion moves into the supplement, Section 3.3 is refocused on prior distillation, and existing appendix material is extensively reordered within a new supplementary structure. These changes exceed ordinary copyediting.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout. The original six-panel qualitative comparison is redistributed between main Figure 3 and supplementary Figure 11, and the guidance-scale illustration moves to the supplement. v3 also transposes the CFG comparison table, expands the main results table, and adds filter plots and Open-Sora/UniCtrl displays.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens assessment of the central consistency, quality, and efficiency claims. Dynamic-degree measurements expose a previously unquantified motion trade-off; the controlled filter ablation tests a key component; and Open-Sora and UniCtrl experiments broaden validation. The shared-VAE limitation makes applicability more explicit. These additions address important evidential gaps in v1, although repeated-run uncertainty and explanations for revised existing scores remain absent.
